title: Public demo
intro.1: The mode behind the live demo on easi.run: anyone gets a short turn with a real browser that can reach only your demo pages.
what-changes-in-demo.title: What changes in demo mode
what-changes-in-demo.1: No password: opening the demo starts a visit at once, at the first site of ADMIN_DEMO_SITES.
what-changes-in-demo.2: Up to ADMIN_MAX_SESSIONS visits run at once, one per client: an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64 network, as Cloudflare’s tunnel reports it. Anyone else waits, and starts as soon as a place is free.
what-changes-in-demo.3: A visit ends at its deadline, whatever happens, or sooner once nobody has watched its browser for 30 seconds; its place is free once its session is confirmed removed.
what-changes-in-demo.4: Visitors can switch between the demos during their visit, and copy and paste go straight to their clipboard.
what-changes-in-demo.5: A recording stops by itself 10 seconds before the visit ends, so its download finishes in time.
what-changes-in-demo.6: Everything an administrator does (more sessions, egresses, settings, agent calls) is refused.
the-admin.title: The admin
the-admin.1: Demo mode uses no egress (its visitors can neither see nor add one), and the admin must be reachable only through the tunnel: it trusts the tunnel’s CF-Connecting-IP header to tell clients apart.
the-admin.2: To show the demo inside your own page, as easi.run’s landing does, name that page’s origin in ADMIN_FRAME_ANCESTORS; nothing else may frame it. ADMIN_STATIC_PATH serves the web client under its own path, so the demo and your page can share one host.
the-walled-garden.title: The walled garden
the-walled-garden.1: The controller sends every address a demo browser asks for to one server you run on an internal Docker network, so no visitor reaches the internet. It refuses to start the walled garden on a network that is not internal.
the-walled-garden.2: That server shows one self-signed certificate for every name, which Chrome accepts by its pinned key: the file CONTROLLER_BENCH_SPKI_FILE names holds the SHA-256 of that public key. easi.run’s own demo (demo/compose.yaml) makes the certificate, its key, and that hash once, with demo/sites-cert.sh, before its first start:
the-walled-garden.3: The controller resolves the session images’ tags once, when it starts. After rebuilding a session image, restart it; this ends the visits under way:
the-walled-garden.4: These settings change what a session may reach and which certificate Chrome accepts. Use them for a demo or a benchmark, never on an installation people use for real browsing.
